solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Organised fight in temporary accommodation, that's clear

indicators.note: in says the organised fight sits within the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is shelter you put up for a short stay
to run something is to organise it; ran is the past tense
to spar is to box or fight

explanation.surface: Someone arranged a brawl in a makeshift shelter, and the matter is plainly settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal, but here it is a synonym of ran, as in ran the show; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something see-through or obvious can be called clear, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Problem getting new start for small person

indicators.note: getting a new start says the first letter of the problem word is swapped for another

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A difficulty is overcome by beginning afresh, for the sake of a little one.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening H of HITCH is replaced by T; the clue does not name the new letter, which the crossers confirm.
explanation.definitionFit: Titch is informal British slang for a very small person, often a child.

clue.text: A first part of timely gift now

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a present is a gift

explanation.surface: A timely gift seems to be wanted right away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at this moment, a synonym of the adverb.

clue.text: Excitedly kiss popular flier

indicators.note: doing something excitedly suggests jumbled, agitated motion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An instruction to kiss a well-liked aviator with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: KISS rearranged gives SISK, then IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A siskin is a small finch, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Do something in law

explanation.surface: Taking action within the bounds of the legal system.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for taking action and a noun for a statute, two separate senses.

clue.text: At outskirts of Essen, German painter, one who's lasted

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the first and last letters

parts.note: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver

explanation.surface: On the edge of Essen, a German artist has survived the ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lasted through hardship is a person who endures, the agent noun.

clue.text: Be honest — order girl to include article on time

indicators.note: to include means the article and time letters are held within the order and girl words

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them
Ruth is a girl's name
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A demand that a young woman write an honest piece on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' means the article and the time abbreviation sit inside the order-plus-girl string, right at the join of its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak without lying is the idiom for being honest.

clue.text: Rob hung jeans out in African city

indicators.note: out means put out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief has hung stolen denims outside in an African metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannesburg is South Africa's largest city.

clue.text: Powerful body's miserable cop-outs

indicators.note: miserable suggests something in a sorry, broken state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mighty organisation is guilty of feeble evasions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprawling, influential organisation with many reaching arms is figuratively called an octopus.

clue.text: Partly glad I thought about such a wave

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
partly says the answer is part of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Someone half pleased at having considered a particular kind of wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partly' shows the letters lie within GLAD I THOUGHT; 'about' says read them backwards, giving TIDAL from ...T IDAL G.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal wave is a recognised kind of wave, so the adjective completes the phrase.

clue.text: Satchel, it's adapted for sport

indicators.note: adapted means changed or modified, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A school bag has been modified for use in games.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field events form a sport.

clue.text: Twenty queue for final result

parts.note: a score is twenty
a line of people waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: Twenty people waiting in line for the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoreline is the final score of a match, its outcome.

clue.text: Humdrum existence of Rugby Union team originally

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: The dull life of a rugby union side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in a dull routine is an idiom for being in a rut.

clue.text: Fellow needing sleep first in Italian port

indicators.note: first says the sleep word goes before the fellow word

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
Les is a man's name, a chap or fellow

explanation.surface: A tired man must rest before anything else in an Italian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a major seaport on Italy's southwest coast.

clue.text: Sound of dog, rising, talented, due now?

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a yap is the sharp bark of a small dog
able means talented or skilled

explanation.surface: A gifted dog's bark rising, and something owed is now due.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: a bill that is payable is due to be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount that must be settled is owed, so it is due for paying.

clue.text: Not refined, bringing rowing gear into Church

indicators.note: bringing one thing into another places the rowing gear inside the church letters
into says the rowing gear goes within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
oars are what rowers use

explanation.surface: A crude person carries boating equipment into a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or unrefined in manner or texture.

clue.text: Safety feature could be bargain? Almost

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become another arrangement
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A car's protective equipment might be a good deal, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims BARGAIN to BARGAI; 'could be' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An airbag inflates in a crash to protect occupants, an example of a safety device.

clue.text: Oddly silky and insidious

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Smooth as silk and subtly harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone cunning and stealthy, synonyms.

clue.text: Cricketer, sympathetic about trouble

indicators.note: about means around, so the sympathetic word goes round the trouble word

parts.note: tender means kind and sympathetic
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A cricket player is kind when someone has a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-ender is one of the weakest batsmen in cricket, who bat last.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender is a type of cricketer, a lower-order batsman.

clue.text: Eat eagerly, like at home

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
in means at home

explanation.surface: Enjoying food heartily, as one does in one's own house.
explanation.definitionFit: To start eating with gusto is the informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Ignoring outsiders, Suzy, with gesture, say, for this Asian

indicators.note: ignoring the outside letters leaves the middle of the name
say signals the gesture word is spoken, giving the same sound with different spelling

parts.note: a beck is a beckoning gesture

explanation.surface: Suzy, set apart, makes a gesture towards someone from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: An Uzbek is a native of Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

clue.text: Man's range of knowledge

definitions.meaning: a man's name, as in Barbie's partner

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a male first name and a noun for the scope of one's understanding.

clue.text: Girl's card game, lost at the end

parts.note: bridge is a card game

indicators.note: at the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A young woman's card game is lost in the final hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridget is a female first name.

clue.text: Some regret nag re-enters village courting couples frequented

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sorry-looking horse returns to a village popular with lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is a Scottish border village where eloping English couples could marry under Scotland's looser laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish village was famous for runaway weddings, so courting couples went there.
